title: Lattices and Functions
summary: The unit connects partial orders with lattices and introduces functions as special relations. It covers bounds, composition, injectivity, surjectivity, inverse functions, operations, and permutations.
keyFacts: A lattice is a partially ordered set in which every pair has a supremum and an infimum.
A complete lattice has a supremum and an infimum for every subset, including the empty set.
In a total order, the supremum of a pair is its maximum and the infimum is its minimum.
The supremum need not belong to the set under consideration; a maximum must belong to it.
In a complete lattice, sup ∅ = min A and inf ∅ = max A.
A total function assigns exactly one element of the codomain to each element of its domain.
A function consists of its rule, its domain, and its codomain.
A k-ary operation on A is a function f: Aᵏ → A.
An operation is associative if parentheses can be omitted when combining terms; commutative if the order can be exchanged; and idempotent if a ◇ a = a.
In g ∘ f, f is applied first, followed by g.
Function composition is associative but not commutative in general.
Injectivity means that each target has at most one preimage; surjectivity means it has at least one preimage.
A function is bijective if and only if every element of its codomain has exactly one preimage.
A function is bijective if and only if its inverse relation is also a function.
A strictly increasing function between totally ordered sets is injective and is bijective as a function onto its image.
For bijective functions, (g ∘ f)⁻¹ = f⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹.
A permutation is a bijective self-map.

review.notes: Alle 33 Fragen geprüft; Antwortmengen und Rechenwege stimmen. Zwei Diagrammkontexte präzisiert: Funktionsmengen gruppiert, Hasse-Relation mit gerichteten Pfeilen dargestellt. Verify-Skripte geprüft.

questions.prompt: What condition makes a partial order a lattice?

options.text: Every element has exactly one predecessor.
Every pair has a supremum and an infimum.
Every element is comparable to every other element.
Every subset has a supremum and an infimum.

questions.explanation: A lattice requires every pair to have a supremum and an infimum. Requiring this for every subset is the condition for a complete lattice.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe a complete lattice? Select all that apply.

options.text: The empty subset is excluded from the condition.
Every subset has a supremum and an infimum.
The condition also applies to infinite subsets.
It is a lattice to begin with.

questions.explanation: A complete lattice is a lattice in which every subset has a supremum and an infimum. This includes the empty set and infinite subsets.

questions.prompt: Every total order is a lattice.
questions.explanation: In a total order, any two elements are comparable. Therefore, the smaller one is their infimum and the larger one is their supremum.

questions.prompt: A total function assigns each $a$ in its domain ___ element of the codomain.
questions.explanation: For a total function, every element of the domain has exactly one image. “At most one” describes a partial function.

questions.prompt: What does the notation $f:A\to B$ specify?

options.text: Only the rule that determines the images.
Only the elements of $B$ that are actually mapped to.

questions.explanation: A function is specified by its rule, domain, and codomain. The notation alone does not imply that it is bijective.

questions.prompt: How many functions are there from a two-element set $A$ to a three-element set $B$?
questions.explanation: Each of the two elements of $A$ has three possible images. Thus, there are $3^2=9$ functions.

questions.prompt: When is a function $f:A^k\to A$ a $k$-ary operation on $A$?

options.text: When it takes just one argument from an arbitrary set.
When it takes $k$ inputs from $A$ and returns a result in $A$.
When it assigns each element of $A$ to an element outside $A$.

questions.explanation: A $k$-ary operation has $A^k$ as its domain and $A$ as its codomain. Thus, its result remains in $A$.

questions.prompt: Which properties does the intersection operation on $2^A$ have? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is not commutative in general.

questions.explanation: Intersection is associative, commutative, and idempotent: $X\cap X=X$. Therefore, option d is false as well.

questions.prompt: In the composition $g\circ f$, ___ is applied first.
questions.explanation: We have $(g\circ f)(a)=g(f(a))$: the inner function $f$ is applied first, followed by $g$.

questions.prompt: Which statements about injectivity, surjectivity, and bijectivity are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Surjective means that every element of the codomain has at least one preimage.
Injective means that every element of the codomain has at most one preimage.
A function is injective if and only if every element of the domain has an image.
Bijective means that every element of the codomain has exactly one preimage.

questions.explanation: These three terms count the preimages of each target element. The property that every domain element has an image is the totality of a function.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, edges point upward to represent the order. Why does the set $\{c,d\}$ have no supremum?

context.content:
graph BT
  c --- a
  c --- b
  d --- a
  d --- b
context.caption: An example of a partial order in which {c,d} has no supremum.

options.text: The two upper bounds $a$ and $b$ are incomparable.

questions.explanation: Both $a$ and $b$ are upper bounds of $c$ and $d$. Since they are incomparable, neither is the least upper bound.

questions.prompt: In the divisibility order on $D_{30}=\{d\in\mathbb N:d\mid 30\}$, what are $\sup\{6,15\}$ and $\inf\{6,15\}$, in that order?
questions.explanation: In the divisibility order, the supremum is the least common multiple and the infimum is the greatest common divisor. For 6 and 15, these are 30 and 3.

questions.prompt: In the order $(2^{\{1,2,3\}},\subseteq)$, determine the pair $(\sup X,\inf X)$ for $X=\{\{1\},\{2\}\}$.
questions.explanation: In the subset order, the supremum is the union and the infimum is the intersection. The union is $\{1,2\}$, and the intersection is empty.

questions.prompt: For $g:\mathbb Z_5\to\mathbb Z_5$ and $g(x)=(2x+1)\bmod 5$, what is $g(2)$?
questions.explanation: $(2\cdot2+1)\bmod 5=5\bmod5=0$.

questions.prompt: A function has the mappings $u\mapsto0$, $v\mapsto0$, and $w\mapsto2$, and codomain $\{0,1,2\}$. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Every element of the codomain is mapped to.

questions.explanation: $u$ and $v$ have the same image, so the function is not injective. The value $1$ is not mapped to; the image is exactly $\{0,2\}$.

questions.prompt: How many surjective functions are there from a three-element set onto a two-element set?
questions.explanation: There are $2^3=8$ functions in total. Two of them map every element to just one of the two target elements; the remaining six are surjective.

questions.prompt: Addition of real numbers is idempotent.
questions.explanation: Idempotence would require $a+a=a$ for every $a$. Even $1+1\ne1$ disproves this.

questions.prompt: Let $f(x)=x+1$ and $g(x)=x^2$. Calculate $(g\circ f)(2)$.
questions.explanation: First calculate $f(2)=3$, then $g(3)=3^2=9$.

questions.prompt: A bijective function $f$ maps $a\mapsto2$, $b\mapsto3$, and $c\mapsto1$. What is $f^{-1}(2)$?
questions.explanation: The inverse function reverses the arrows. Since $f(a)=2$, we have $f^{-1}(2)=a$.

questions.prompt: What is the arity of a function $h:A\times B\times C\to A$ when its inputs are written as arguments?
questions.explanation: The domain contains tuples with three components. Therefore, the function has three arguments and is ternary.

questions.prompt: A partial function on $A=\{1,2,3\}$ has the mappings $1\mapsto x$ and $3\mapsto y$. To make it total, a new symbol $\bot$ is added to the codomain. Which pair is added?
questions.explanation: Only the element $2$ had no image yet. When the function is made total, it is assigned the new target symbol $\bot$.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, the elements on the left form the domain $A$, and those on the right form the codomain $B$. Which statement is correct?

context.content:

  subgraph A
    p
    q
    r
  end
  subgraph B
    u
    v
    w
  end
  p --> u
  q --> v
  r --> v
context.caption: Arrows of the mapping from A to B

options.text: It is a surjective function from $A$ to $B$.
It is an injective function from $A$ to $B$.
It is a total function from $A$ to $B$.
It is a bijective function from $A$ to $B$.

questions.explanation: Every element of $A$ has exactly one outgoing arrow, so the mapping is a total function. It is not injective because both $q$ and $r$ point to $v$, and it is not surjective because $w$ has no incoming arrow.

questions.prompt: In the divisibility order on $D_{30}$, what holds for $X=\{2,3\}$?

options.text: $\sup X$ does not exist because $2$ and $3$ are incomparable.

questions.explanation: The least common multiple of 2 and 3 is 6, so it is their supremum. Since 6 is not in $X$, $X$ has no maximum.

questions.prompt: Every finite lattice is complete.
questions.explanation: In a finite lattice, a supremum and an infimum can be formed for every subset, including the empty subset.

questions.prompt: In a complete lattice with least element $\min A$, $\sup\emptyset=___$ holds.
questions.explanation: Every element is an upper bound of the empty set, since there is nothing to check. The least of these bounds is $\min A$.

questions.prompt: To make a partial function total, one can add a new target symbol $\bot$ and map every element without an image to it.
questions.explanation: The new symbol is added to the codomain. This gives each element that previously had no image exactly one image.

questions.prompt: Two identical mapping rules always describe the same function, even if their domains or codomains differ.
questions.explanation: A function consists of its rule, domain, and codomain. Therefore, the same rule with different sets can define a different function or may not be defined on those sets.

questions.prompt: A function is bijective if and only if its inverse relation is a function from $B$ to $A$.
questions.explanation: When the arrows are reversed, each element of $B$ must have exactly one successor in $A$. This is precisely what it means for $f$ to be bijective.

questions.prompt: If $f$ is strictly increasing between totally ordered sets, then $f$ is injective and bijective as a function onto $f(A)$.
questions.explanation: Strict increase prevents two distinct inputs from having the same image. Moreover, $f$ is surjective onto its image, and therefore bijective.

questions.prompt: Which statements about injectivity of a composition hold in general? Select all that apply.

options.text: If $g\circ f$ is injective, then $f$ is injective.
If $f$ is injective, then $g\circ f$ is always injective.
If $g\circ f$ is injective, then $g$ is also injective.
If $f$ and $g$ are injective, then $g\circ f$ is injective.

questions.explanation: The composition of two injective functions is injective. Conversely, if the composition is injective, the inner function $f$ must be injective; this does not follow for $g$.

questions.prompt: Which statements about surjectivity of a composition hold in general? Select all that apply.

options.text: If $f$ and $g$ are surjective, then $g\circ f$ is surjective.
If $g\circ f$ is surjective, then $g$ is surjective.
If $g\circ f$ is surjective, then $f$ is also surjective.
If $g$ is surjective, then $g\circ f$ is always surjective.

questions.explanation: The composition of surjective functions is surjective. If the composition is surjective, the outer function $g$ must be surjective; this does not follow for $f$.

questions.prompt: For the bijective functions $f(x)=x+3$ and $g(x)=2x$ on $\mathbb R$, which mapping is $(g\circ f)^{-1}$?
questions.explanation: $(g\circ f)(x)=2x+6$. Solving $y=2x+6$ for $x$ gives $x=y/2-3$.

questions.prompt: The arrows form a self-map of $\mathbb Z_5$. Which description of its cycles is correct?

context.caption: Arrows of the self-map on ℤ₅.

options.text: One cycle of length 3 and two fixed points.
One cycle of length 4 and one fixed point.
Two cycles of length 2 and one fixed point.

questions.explanation: Following the arrows gives $0\to1\to3\to2\to0$. Also, 4 is a fixed point because $4\to4$.

questions.prompt: In $D_{30}$ with the divisibility order, determine the pair $(\sup X,\inf X)$ for $X=\{6,15\}$ and decide whether $X$ has a maximum.
questions.explanation: The least common multiple is 30 and the greatest common divisor is 3. The supremum 30 is not in $X$, so there is no maximum.

questions.prompt: How many functions and how many bijections are there from a three-element set onto a two-element set?
questions.explanation: There are $2^3=8$ functions. A bijection between finite sets of equal size would require both sets to have the same size; here they differ, so there are none.

questions.prompt: On $\mathbb Z_5$, let $f(x)=(2x+1)\bmod5$ and $g(y)=3(y-1)\bmod5$. Which statement is correct?

options.text: $g\circ f=\mathrm{Id}$ and $f\circ g=\mathrm{Id}$; therefore, $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.

questions.explanation: Substitution gives $g(f(x))=3(2x)\equiv x\pmod5$ and $f(g(y))=6y-5\equiv y\pmod5$. Thus, both functions are bijective and are inverses of each other.

questions.prompt: Let $f,g\in S_A$, so they are bijective self-maps of $A$. Which functions are also guaranteed to belong to $S_A$? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The identity is bijective, the inverse of a bijection is bijective, and the composition of bijections is bijective. Here, addition of functions is not defined as an operation on permutations.

questions.prompt: In the complete lattice order $(2^{\{a,b\}},\subseteq)$, what are $\sup\emptyset$ and $\inf\emptyset$?
questions.explanation: The least element of the subset order is $\emptyset$ and the greatest is $\{a,b\}$. Therefore, for the empty set, $\sup\emptyset=\min A$ and $\inf\emptyset=\max A$.

questions.prompt: For the union operation $\cup$ on $2^A$, which statements hold? Select all that apply.

options.text: $X\cup Y$ generally depends on the order of the sets.

questions.explanation: Union is associative, commutative, and idempotent. Changing the order of its arguments does not change the result.

questions.prompt: The function $f:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ with $f(x)=x^2$ is bijective and has inverse function $x\mapsto\sqrt{x}$.
questions.explanation: Squaring is bijective on the nonnegative real numbers. The square root maps each target to its unique preimage.

questions.prompt: An arrow $x\to y$ means $(x,y)\in R$. A pair $(x,z)$ belongs to $R^2$ if and only if there is an element $y$ such that $x\to y$ and $y\to z$ both hold. Which pairs belong to $R^2$?

questions.explanation: The two-arrow paths are $p\to q\to r$, $q\to r\to r$, and $r\to r\to r$. The arrow $p\to s$ contributes to no two-arrow path because no arrow leaves $s$.

questions.explanation: The edge $x\to z$ is transitive because $x\to y$ and $y\to z$ are already present. Hasse diagrams omit transitive edges.

questions.prompt: On $\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$, let $x\sim y$ hold exactly when $x$ and $y$ are congruent modulo $3$. Which set is the equivalence class of $1$?
questions.explanation: In the given set, exactly 1 and 4 are congruent to 1 modulo 3. They form the equivalence class of 1.

levels.title: In Practice: Lattices and Functions in Everyday Life

questions.prompt: Alice has the permissions {Read, Export}, and Ben has {Read, Modify}. In the lattice of all subsets of these permissions, ordered by inclusion, which set contains both roles while adding as few permissions as possible?

options.text: The supremum, that is, the union
The infimum, that is, the intersection

questions.explanation: For sets ordered by inclusion, the union is the least upper bound and hence the supremum: {Read, Export, Modify}.

questions.prompt: In a compiler pipeline, $f$ translates source code into a syntax tree. Then $g$ simplifies that syntax tree. Which composition correctly describes this order?
questions.explanation: In $g \circ f$, $f$ is applied first, followed by $g$. This matches the stated order: first create the syntax tree, then simplify it.

questions.prompt: A smart home panel displays four distinguishable sensors. Each sensor can independently report exactly one of three states. How many different complete state profiles are possible?
questions.explanation: Each of the four sensors has three possible states. Thus, there are $3^4 = 81$ complete profiles, which is also the number of functions from the four sensors to the three-element set of states.

questions.prompt: Three students are assigned to courses L1 through L4: Mia → L1, Noah → L2, Sam → L3. The domain consists of exactly these three students; the codomain is {L1, L2, L3, L4}. Which property does this mapping have?
questions.explanation: Different students map to different courses, so the function is injective. L4 is not mapped to, so it is not surjective onto the given codomain.

questions.prompt: A letter substitution assigns each letter of the alphabet A–Z to exactly one letter from A–Z. Each letter from A–Z occurs exactly once as an output. What is this mapping called?
questions.explanation: The mapping is a bijective function from A–Z onto A–Z. Such a self-map of a set is called a permutation and has an inverse function.

questions.prompt: A permission system has eight individual permissions. How many different permission profiles can a role have if it may have none or all of them?
questions.explanation: Each of the eight permissions is either included or not included. The number of profiles is therefore the cardinality of the power set: $2^8 = 256$.

questions.prompt: A cloud service takes the union of keyword sets when messages arrive from two devices. A message may arrive again. Which property of union ensures that taking the union with the same set again changes nothing?
questions.explanation: Union is idempotent: for every set $X$, $X \cup X = X$ holds. Therefore, taking the union with the same keyword set again does not change the result.

questions.prompt: A device can send a sequence of exactly twelve bit positions. Each position is either 0 or 1. How many different bit patterns are possible?
questions.explanation: Each of the twelve positions has two possibilities. Thus, there are $2^{12} = 4096$ patterns; each pattern corresponds to a function from the twelve positions to $\{0,1\}$.

questions.prompt: A dashboard should display the highest value actually measured in a data series: $18{,}2$, $20{,}1$, and $19{,}4$ °C. Which term describes this value?
questions.explanation: The maximum is the greatest value that actually occurs in the data series. For this finite set in the usual numerical order, it is also the supremum.

questions.prompt: A shop API assigns exactly one status from the codomain {open, shipped, delivered, cancelled} to each order ID in the domain {A17, A18, A19}: A17 → shipped, A18 → open, A19 → delivered. What is this mapping?

options.text: A permutation of the status values
A binary operation on order IDs
A total function from order IDs to status values
A partial function because “cancelled” does not occur

questions.explanation: Each order ID in the domain has exactly one status from the codomain. The mapping is therefore a total function. The fact that “cancelled” is not mapped to only means that the function is not surjective onto the given codomain.
